data.gender_notes: Karitina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'karat', meaning 'to refine'. In the Bible, Karitina is a variant of the name Mary, symbolizing purity, holiness, and enlightenment. The name Karitina carries the meaning “Pure, Holy, Light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Karitina usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, holy, light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A beacon of light, shining through love and faith.
data.etymology: Karitina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Holy, Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karitina total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: קאריטינה
in_hebrew.meaning: קאריטינה נגזר מקריתוס ומשמעותו חסד או אהבה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קאריטינה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו ביוונית ונגזר מהמילה 'כריטוס' (Χαρίτος) שמשמעותה חסד או אהבה. השם קאריטינה משמש כנש衍 לשם היווני χαριτινος, שפירושו 'מלא חסד' או 'אהוב'. השם מופיע במסורת הנוצרית כסמל לאהבה וחסד אלוהיים.

in_greek.name: Καριτίνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καριτίνα προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'Χαρίτος' (Cháris) που σημαίνει χάρη ή αγάπη. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η λέξη 'χάρις' (cháris) αναφέρεται στη θεία χάρη και αγάπη. Η Καριτίνα είναι σύμβολο της πνευματικής αγάπης και χάρης που προσφέρει ο Θεός.

in_latin.name: Caritina
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Caritina originates from the Latin word 'caritas,' meaning charity or love. In Christian tradition, Caritina represents the virtue of love and charity. The name gained popularity in medieval Europe as a symbol of spiritual devotion and selfless love.

in_english.name: Karitina
in_english.long_meaning: The name Karitina has its roots in the Greek word 'Χαρίτος' (Cháris), meaning grace or love. Historically, the name has been used across various Christian cultures, reflecting its universal appeal and significance.

historical_references.reference: Karitina of Portugal, also known as Catherine of Braganca, was a Portuguese princess and Queen consort of France from 1662 to 1680. Born on December 24, 1646, in Sintra, Portugal, she was the eldest daughter of the Duke of Braganca and the heiress to the House of Braganca. She married King Louis XIV of France in 1660, despite her father's objections, and bore him seven children. Her marriage was a significant political alliance as it ended the long-standing rivalry between France and Portugal.

historical_references.reference: Saint Catherine of Alexandria, a legendary early Christian saint and martyr, is believed to have lived during the 4th century AD. According to tradition, she was a learned woman who converted many to Christianity and was tortured and executed under the Roman Emperor Maxentius. Her feast day is celebrated on November 25.
